subject: GlacierAI post-call: latency & throughput commitments + next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@glacierai.com>, Tess Nguyen <tess@glacierai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GlacierAI post-call: latency & throughput commitments + next steps

Hi Samir / Tess —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick write-up of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of customer goals / pain points
- Primary: real-time document enrichment API for legal workflows (90% of calls <= 150ms p95 for 256-token responses).
- Secondary: embedding generation for semantic search (batchable, throughput-sensitive).
- Constraint: models must remain in customer VPC for PII; logging/audit trail required.

Key constraints & numbers you shared
- Peak QPS expected: 60 sustained, spikes to 200 for 10–20 minute windows.
- Typical request size: 32–512 tokens (median ~180).
- SLA expectation: 99.9% availability; target cold-start tails <250ms.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Deployment topology: private Redwood Private control plane + VPC-injected serving nodes in their account.
- Model family: 13B quantized variants for real-time path; 70B for batched offline embeddings where cost allows.
- Autoscale policy: baseline pool sized for 60 QPS, burst pool for spikes with fast warmup and pre-warming options.
- Observability: per-route latency percentiles + token-level cost breakdown in Console; audit logs forwarded to GlacierAI SIEM.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
1) You: send representative traffic sample and worst-case payloads (Samir) — by 2026-07-19. (attachment referenced)
2) Redwood: follow-up technical note with recommended instance topology and estimated reserved capacity cost (Neha + Karthik) — by 2026-07-20.
3) Arrange deep technical call with Glacier infra + engineers — propose Tue/Wed next week; Redwood to propose slots.

Attachments I referenced: load profile CSV and example payloads (please attach your redaction guidelines if any).

If that matches your understanding, a quick reply with a thumbs-up (or corrections) and Samir’s traffic dump will let us move the topology estimate forward.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

My takeaways for engineering: 
- Real-time enrichment: to hit 150ms p95 for ~180-token median, we should plan for: optimized 13B quantized model with KV cache reuse, dedicated pre-warmed pool to avoid cold-starts, and continuous batching with strict per-request latency cap.
- Autoscaling: baseline pool to cover 60 QPS assuming average tokens per request; add fast-burst pool scaled by token-s/sec budget. We should include a fallback route to a slightly smaller model if burst capacity unavailable (graceful degradation).
- Embeddings: recommend a separate batch-only cluster with throughput-optimized instances and integrated batching (no strict latency SLO). Provide TTL and caching for repeated vectors.
- Compliance: require VPC peering + KMS integration; logs must be retained for 365 days and exported to Glacier’s SIEM.

Action for you two: can you produce a rough instance topology (node types, counts, and a cost ballpark) and a list of technical follow-up Qs by EOD Monday? I’ll consolidate and send to Samir for the Tues call.

Thanks — Neha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: GlacierAI post-call: latency & throughput commitments + next steps

Neha / Marissa / Samir —

Thanks for sharing the sample traffic; reviewed the histograms and ran a quick back-of-envelope. High-level recommendations and open questions below.

Technical summary / proposed topology
- Real-time pathway (strict p95 150ms target):
  - Model: 13B quantized (int8 or bfloat16 depending on customer HW).
  - Serving: 3 pre-warmed nodes (A100-equivalent) handling steady-state 60 QPS with KV cache pinned per session; 2 additional warm standby nodes for burst to 200 QPS (fast warm-up via cached model shards).
  - Batching: max batch size configured at 8 for low-latency path; continuous micro-batching to fill at 10–15ms windows.
  - Fallback: smaller 7B quantized variant for degraded latency path; automatic quality gates in Console to detect regressions.

- Embeddings pathway (cost-sensitive, high-throughput):
  - Separate batch cluster (V100/RTX-class) with async worker pool; support 10k–100k vector jobs within 15-minute windows.
  - Recommend using mixed-precision to lower token cost and increase throughput.

Estimated capacity & cost ballpark (monthly)
- Reserved capacity commit: baseline 3 serving nodes + 2 warm standby for peak -> estimated $XXk/month (placeholder; will refine once we confirm instance class).
- Batch cluster: variable; estimate $YYk/month for expected monthly vector volume (needs exact vector counts).

Open technical questions for GlacierAI (please confirm):
1) Do you have a preferred instance family in your VPC (e.g., A100 vs H100)?
2) Are there maximum allowed egress costs / bandwidth caps we should account for?
3) Any tokenization/custom model adapters already in use (we saw hints in sample payload)? If so, share tokenizer and model variant.
4) Retention: confirm 365 days for audit logs and whether logs must be encrypted with customer KMS.

Next steps (concrete)
- Redwood: produce a 1-page topology sketch + cost ranges (this week; Neha/Karthik).
- GlacierAI: confirm instance family and share any redaction automation before Tue call (Samir).
- Schedule deep-technical call for Tue 2026-07-21 12:30 PT (Neha to send invite).

I'll follow with a short diagram and numbers by EOD Monday.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
